name: Richardson v. United States
summary: The Court required unanimous jury agreement on the specific underlying acts constituting elements of a continuing criminal enterprise offense, distinguishing between elements of a crime (requiring unanimity) and means of committing a crime (not requiring unanimity).
significance: Held that jurors must unanimously agree on which specific violations make up a 'continuing series of violations' under a federal drug statute, supporting the argument that unanimity extends beyond the general verdict to specific factual findings.
